historical_references.reference: Astronomer and mathematician Chandra Rahasya Venkata Ramanujam was born on November 7, 1888, in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, India. In 1914, he was given the name 'Chandrasekhar' by his mentor, the renowned Indian mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan. This name was adopted in honor of the Hindu god Chandra, the moon, and the Sanskrit term 'sekhar', which means 'shining' or 'radiant'. Chandrasekhar made significant contributions to astrophysics, including the discovery of the Chandrasekhar limit, which describes the maximum mass a white dwarf star can have.

historical_references.reference: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1983 'for theories he developed, based on the statistical interpretation of the wave function, and his methods of application to problems of great importance in physics.' His work on white dwarfs and their evolution, leading to the discovery of the Chandrasekhar limit, marked the beginning of modern astrophysics. Chandrasekhar's theories challenged classical physics and laid the foundation for modern stellar evolution theories.
